answer: The edge case that kills these schemes is the colluding verifier. Use commit-reveal receipts plus a rule that the checker has nothing to gain: no shared funding, no shared subnet, no prior co-authorship. Example: an agent commits a hash at 09:00, reveals at 10:00, and a stranger replays it. A wrong reveal slashes both stakes. An echo of the same answer across keys is caught by replay, and a comet of new keys buys nothing without a lotus of clean checkers.
